newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs rebound to end up led by CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs rebound to end up led by CVRD.

text.p: Local stocks ended strongly higher in a broad technical rebound, led by a jump in Cia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) after Brazil's high court struck down a legal challenge to the firm's privatization, brokers said.
"One important factor (in the day's rise) was the high court's decision," one local trader told Reuters. "It would seem to leave CVRD ready for the sale."
The Sao Paulo bourse's Bovespa .BVSP index of 49 most- traded shares closed up 1.69 percent at 9,634 points on healthy trade of 521 million reais ($492 million).

Brokers said the bolsa rose from the opening bell in a rebound after the settlement of options on Tuesday lifted downward pressure and cleared the way Wednesday for share prices to rise to more reasonable levels.
"It was a technical rebound after options expired," said a local dealer, adding that the recovery was aided by stock price rises on Wall Street.
Telebras' preferred rise 1.71 percent to close at 119.00 reais, while its common voter surged 2.71 percent to end at 113.49 reais.
But CVRD, which saw volume of more than $45 million, led the rally, with its preferred share jumping 3.69 percent to end at 26.70 reais, while its common voter closed flat at 29.90 reais.

The miner was higher throughout the day, despite a flood of lawsuits seeking to derail the government's April 29 auction of a maximum 45 percent voting stake. But it received a strong boost late in the session when the court threw out a legal challange by the Organization of Brazilian Attorneys (OAB), which filed a suit claiming the sale was unconstitutional.

Brazilian power stocks accompanied the rise, albeit at a mellower pace. The bolsa's Electrical Energy Index .IEE rose 0.86 percent to end at 2,665 points, led by a 1.03 percent rise in Eletrobras' preferred.
Preferred shares of Minas Gerais state-owned Cemig rose 0.65 percent to end at 46.70 reais.
State oil monopoly Petrobras' preferred also rose strongly, ending 1.9 percent higher at 214.50 reais.
